title: Common benchmark dataset
$comment: B1 defines this schema. The 150-question dataset itself does not exist yet; this file only fixes the shape any future dataset author (or generator) must follow, mirroring benchmark/evaluator/models.py (BenchmarkItem, EvidenceRef) exactly.
description: A benchmark dataset is either a bare JSON array of items, or an object carrying that array under 'items' or 'questions'.

forbiddenKeys.description: System-internal identifiers that must never appear in the common ground truth. Allowing chunk_id / vector_id / node_id (or any per-system alias of them) here would let one system's chunking or indexing decisions leak into the shared gold standard, making cross-system comparison unfair. Mirrors models.FORBIDDEN_DATASET_KEYS exactly.

benchmarkItem.description: One benchmark question plus its architecture-neutral ground truth. Ground truth is expressed only as document/article/clause/point/text, never as a system-internal id.

id.description: Unique question id. Must be non-empty and unique across the dataset.

category.description: Question category, used for macro-averaging. No fixed enum: the evaluator reads categories from the data.

answerable.description: Whether the question has a correct, answerable response in-scope (false marks a deliberately unanswerable / out-of-scope question).

question.description: The question text shown to systems under test.

gold_markers.description: Free-text markers a correct answer should contain. Placeholder strings starting with '<' (e.g. '<fill in the correct answer>') are dropped by the loader and should be treated as absent.

gold_claims.description: Atomic gold claims the answer should support, for claim-level scoring.

gold_evidence.description: Authoritative evidence a correct answer must rest on. Entries with required=false are acceptable but not necessary.

evidenceRef.description: One piece of evidence, located by document/article/clause/point rather than by any system's internal chunk or node id. 'text' is mandatory; 'clause' and 'point' are diagnostic labels and do not participate in comparative scoring.

document_id.description: Identifier of the legal document (e.g. a law/decree number), not a system chunk id.

article.description: Article ('Điều'). Integers are accepted here for authoring convenience and are coerced to strings by the Python loader (models._as_opt_str). Together with document_id this is the scoring depth: a declared mismatch here is a hard negative.

clause.description: Clause ('khoản'). Integers are accepted and coerced to strings by the Python loader. Recorded for error analysis only: a clause mismatch never makes evidence support false, because systems declare clause metadata at different granularities and penalising the ones that declare it would be an unfair asymmetry.

point.description: Point ('điểm'). Integers are accepted and coerced to strings by the Python loader. Diagnostic only, exactly like 'clause'.

text.description: Verbatim evidence text, required. It is the common arbiter every system can reach: a system that declares no article or clause metadata can still be credited through text matching, so gold without text would silently favour whichever system reports the richest metadata.

required.description: Whether this evidence is necessary (true, default) or merely acceptable (false). Hit@k and MRR use required evidence only; Evidence Recall reports both.
